Celestial Frontier — Synthetic Tester Report

A 1,000-session automated tester fleet, a clean 21-device responsive sweep, and 12 deep persona playthroughs run against build v1.7.0 (4264b2e). Every issue below was reproduced against the running game or verified in source before it was written down.

1000 bot sessions 21 device profiles 12 persona playthroughs 49 distinct issues generated 2026-07-26 08:29 UTC

What the score means. Fun factor is a judgement made by each persona from a full storyboard of their own session, not a formula. The fleet computes a separate behavioural proxy from measured session properties (reward density, progression, breadth, friction, continuity, onboarding cost) — reported further down and deliberately kept apart from the human-style ratings.

Issues49 distinct, ranked by severity then how many testers hit them

An issue found by several independent personas on different devices is a stronger signal than one found once. Reporter counts are shown on the right of each row.

critical Toasts cover the navigation, the control hint, and whichever panel just opened layout 6 testers · 6 devices
Evidence
State 05, the first live gameplay screen: two stacked toasts occupy roughly y 640-796, x 56-375. The five-button nav row sits at y ~776. Only a sliver of the leftmost chip is visible. The control hint 'Tap a planet to survey it, pinch in to land' at y ~733 is ghosted behind the toast. State 08 shows the same toasts covering nearly the whole Star Atlas sheet.
Impact
A player who skips Field Training arrives with zero instruction and zero navigation visible. I did not know the Compendium, Shipyard, Atlas or Charters existed.
Suggested fix
Reserve a toast lane that stops above the bottom chrome on viewports under 420px, cap the visible stack at one, and queue the rest to the bell tray. The arrival burst is 4 toasts in 5 seconds - collapse to one.
Reported by
skimmer on iphone-15-pro
Evidence
State 08. The Atlas occupies only the bottom ~28% of the 915px viewport (y~631-760). Its single Earth row and that row's TRAVEL/FAVORITE/HOME links are covered by the CHARTER COMPLETE toast; GROUND SURVEY covers the rest. The only visible Atlas UI is the filter chip row.
Impact
I opened a board and it showed me nothing, and the toasts are opaque and on top, so tapping the Earth row hits the toast. My conclusion is the Atlas is empty and not worth reopening.
Suggested fix
Suppress or collapse the toast stack while a board is open, and give the Atlas a taller default height under 500px width.
Reported by
button-masher on pixel-7
Evidence
08-atlas: the Atlas opens and all that is visible is the chip row; everything below is covered by two stacked toasts. 03 and 04: the WELCOME toast covers the on-map hint and the entire bottom pill row. 05: two toasts occupy the bottom 25%.
Impact
At 344px the toasts are wider than the panels they land on, so a freshly-opened Star Atlas looks empty rather than covered - and during Field Training the toast hides the controls the training is telling me to use.
Suggested fix
When a panel is open, dock toasts to the top under the HP row, or cap the visible stack at one under 420px and route the rest to the tray.

critical The game board is unreachable by keyboard or assistive technology accessibility 1 tester · 1 device
Evidence
The hint bar in every system-map frame (03, 04, 05, 06, 08, 09, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16) reads 'Hover a planet to preview · click to survey · scroll in to land'. Frame 06 is labelled survey-card yet shows no survey card at all — it is identical to 05 apart from toasts — and 07-planetside is absent from this device's storyboard entirely, so the automated run never landed. Source confirms why: /root/cf/src/celestialfrontier.github.io-main/index.html registers only pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup/wheel/touchstart/touchmove/touchend/click on the canvas (lines 5070-5188, 12125); zoom exists solely as cv.addEventListener('wheel', ...) at 5162; and the strings ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft and ArrowRight do not appear once in 23,972 lines. HINTS at 2166-2172 also gives 'Scroll out to leave this world' as the only exit from a surface, and there is no Depart/Leave button in the DOM. Travelling from the Star Atlas does not help: goTo() at 14684 opens with 'stickyPick=null; locked=null;', so arriving at a world leaves no survey card and therefore no Land button.
Impact
A keyboard-only player can name an explorer, open every panel, and read every word of lore — and can never survey a world, never land, never move the camera. The entire game is behind a mouse. This is not a degraded experience; it is a total block on the primary function.
Suggested fix
Give the canvas tabindex="0" and a roving keyboard focus over the existing picks[] array: Left/Right (or Tab within the board) cycles bodies nearest-first, Enter surveys (the same path a click takes, so it earns survey credit), Escape releases the lock. Bind +/- and PageUp/PageDown to zoomAt() centred on the focused body so 'scroll in to land' has a key, and arrow keys with a modifier to pan curCam(). Add an explicit 'Leave this world' button to the surface-mode survey card rather than relying on scroll-out. Then rewrite HINTS to name the keys alongside the pointer verbs.
Reported by
accessibility on desktop-1080
Evidence
index.html:2115-2120 — a comment about Edge renderer crashes, then: try{ cv.setAttribute('aria-hidden','true'); cv.setAttribute('role','presentation'); }catch(_){ }. The canvas is the whole game: the star, the eight worlds, orbits, comets and the ship. There is no textual mirror of it anywhere — the file contains zero aria-live regions (grep for aria-live returns nothing), so the toast stream visible bottom-right in frames 03-16 and the notification tray in frame 16 are never announced either.
Impact
A screen-reader user is told, authoritatively, that the play area is decorative and contains nothing. Combined with the pointer-only input, the game is not merely hard to use with a screen reader — it is invisible to one, and every piece of feedback the game gives (survey results, charter progress, landing outcomes) passes silently.
Suggested fix
Keep the canvas out of the a11y tree if the Edge crash is real, but pair it with a visually-hidden live region that mirrors the board: a list of the currently pickable objects (name, type, distance) rebuilt when picks[] changes, and an aria-live="polite" region fed by toast() at index.html:14970 so every toast is announced once. That also fixes the notification tray, which already has the text.
Reported by
accessibility on desktop-1080
major Prime Codex truncates all nine titans mid-word readability 7 testers · 9 devices
Evidence
13-prime-codex: every one of the nine Signature rows reads '📡 a resonance beyond your charter — build toward the stars to h…' immediately followed on the next line by 'relic blueprint on the claim', so it scans as one broken run-on sentence. The cause is in the source: .psig .psub2 is styled 'white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis' (index.html:1082), the resonance string ends '…to hear it.' (index.html:21952), and 'relic blueprint on the claim' is a separate sibling .psub2 div (index.html:21981). I confirmed the identical truncation in desktop-1440__13-prime-codex.png, so this is not specific to the tall layout — it reproduces everywhere the string exceeds the row width, which is all nine rows on both devices I checked.
Impact
The Prime Codex is the screen that explains what the entire game is for — nine titans, nine elements. It is the one place a new player goes to find out what they are ultimately meant to do, and every line of guidance on it is cut off before it finishes the sentence. I closed it none the wiser and slightly suspicious that the game was broken.
Suggested fix
Let .psig .psub2 wrap to two lines (-webkit-line-clamp:2, white-space:normal) instead of single-line ellipsis, or shorten the locked resonance copy so it fits — e.g. 'beyond your charter — build toward the stars.'
Reported by
cautious-newbie on surface-pro
Evidence
13-prime-codex: all nine rows clip mid-word. The clue line under each is clipped too, then a third line renders in full, so the row looks complete while the informative lines are cut. Source line 1082: .psig .psub2{white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis} with no narrow-screen relaxation, even though a @media (max-width:380px) block exists at line 1476 and only touches #searchin, #hpbar and #chbtn.
Impact
The Prime Codex is the stated win condition and the only bounded list in an infinite universe. On the narrowest phone it degrades into nine rows of ellipses, and the clipped clue is what tells you whether a titan is reachable now.
Suggested fix
Inside the existing @media (max-width:380px) block override .psig .psub2 to white-space:normal, or keep a clamp at -webkit-line-clamp:2 so the guardian's full name always lands.
Reported by
completionist on galaxy-fold
Evidence
13-prime-codex. All nine signature rows render the identical line 'a resonance beyond your charter — build toward the stars to h...' with an orphaned second line 'relic blueprint on the claim' beneath. Source: `.psig .psub2` is `white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis` (line 1082); the full string is 'a resonance beyond your charter — build toward the stars to hear it.' (line 21952), rendered as a separate div from the relic line (line 21981).
Impact
This is the game's headline goal — nine titans, 0/9 sitting in the top bar of every screen. The only text explaining why they are locked is cut off on a tablet, and once I mentally complete the sentence I find it is the same sentence nine times. Nine named titans with wonderful names (Zephyrmaw, the Stellar Squall; Abyssleth, the Tide Devout) and not one word about where any of them is. It reads like placeholder copy under a gorgeous frame.
Suggested fix
Let `.psub2` wrap: `white-space:normal; display:-webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp:2`. Then give each signature its own resonance line naming a direction or depth — 'Terrakoth waits on a heavy world close to home; Nullreth past the Deep Field' — so the Codex doubles as a map instead of a checklist.
Reported by

major Panels, docks and popovers render over the survey card instead of replacing it layout 6 testers · 7 devices
Evidence
States 08, 09, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16. The bottom bar has no background fill, so the Mercury survey card renders through it. Magnified crop of state 12 shows 'MINERAL VEINS' overlapping the Charters icon and '1,507 pulls left' running across four chips. Not one of 16 frames shows the nav bar cleanly legible.
Impact
This bar is the only route to Atlas, Compendium, Shipyard, Charters and Prime Codex at this size. A first-time player who cannot read it cannot navigate the game.
Suggested fix
Give the bottom bar a solid backdrop on narrow viewports and reserve its height as bottom padding on #panel so the survey card scrolls above it.

cautious-newbie on iphone-se
Evidence
State 08: the Star Atlas is an untitled ~135px band across mid-screen with the Mercury card fully visible and undimmed above and below. State 09 the same. States 12 and 16 slice a list row in half at the panel border. Shipyard (10) and Prime Codex (13) by contrast are proper titled full-screen panels.
Impact
No title, no scrim, previous screen still readable around it - impossible to tell what you opened or which layer the next tap hits.

Below ~420px, promote Atlas, Compendium, Charters, Records and Notifications to full-height titled sheets with a dimmed scrim, matching Shipyard and Prime Codex.

cautious-newbie on iphone-se
Evidence
11-records: the Records panel opens over the right side of the Mercury survey card, hiding the LAND, MINE DEPOSITS and PLANETSIDE buttons entirely and covering the Spectral Class and Biome values; it also runs to the bottom edge of the viewport with the ENGINEERING achievement row sliced in half. 16-notifications does the same thing over the same card. 14-settings covers the '+ ADD TO STAR ATLAS' label. Meanwhile the panels use two different models with no rule I could learn: Compendium (09) and Star Atlas (08) open as small corner popovers with the world still live behind them, while Shipyard (10) and Prime Codex (13) open as large centred modals with the whole screen dimmed.
Impact
When the card I was reading vanishes under a panel I just opened, my first thought is not 'that's a stacking order', it's 'did I close something? did I lose it?' And because half the panels dim the world and half don't, there is no single gesture I can learn for 'put this back the way it was' — which is the one skill a cautious player wants before touching anything else.
Suggested fix
At 912px wide there is a completely empty left column — dock Records, Notifications and Settings there instead of into the same right gutter the survey card occupies, or push the survey card left when a right-side panel opens. Constrain panel height to the viewport minus the dock so no row is sliced. Pick one panel model (dim-and-modal, or popover) and use it for all of them.

major Records journal renders as one run-on string ("Mercurycarbon · 7/26") layout 5 testers · 5 devices
Evidence
11-records shows 'Mercurycarbon - 7/26' with no separator and no dim label colour. renderRecords() emits <div class="srow"><span class="k">Mercury</span><span>carbon - 7/26</span></div>, but the only rules are #stats .srow and #stats .srow .k at lines 371-372. #stats lives inside #sheetstats while #records is a separate top-level panel - a leftover from the v1.5.2 move of the trophy room into its own rail panel. The same markup backs the 17-row Statistics ledger.
Impact
The journal is the record of everywhere I have set foot and it reads as a nonsense word. All 17 Statistics rows are built the same way - the exact ledger a completionist opens first.
Suggested fix
Change selectors at 371-372 to '#stats .srow, #records .srow' or move the rules to a bare .srow class.
Reported by
completionist on galaxy-fold
Evidence
11-records, under the EXPEDITION JOURNAL heading, the single entry reads 'Mercurycarbon · 7/26'. Source: the journal row is built as two spans inside `<div class="srow">` (line ~23580) writing the world name and the rolled landing region key, but the only flex rule for that class is `#stats .srow{display:flex;justify-content:space-between}` (line 371). The Records panel is `#records` (line 1405) and has no `.srow` rule, so the spans render inline with no gap or separator. The Statistics block inside Records uses the same `.srow` markup, so every stat row ('Living worlds surveyed' + count) will run together the same way once expanded.
Impact
The Expedition Journal is precisely the feature I would live in — 'one line per landing, world and region and when'. My very first entry is already unreadable, and it makes the whole trophy room look unfinished. Fixing this also silently fixes the entire Statistics ledger.
Suggested fix
Change the selector to `#stats .srow, #records .srow` (or move the rule to a shared class). Format the entry so the region is legible and title-cased: 'Mercury · Carbon flats · 7/26'.
Reported by
explorer on ipad-mini
Evidence
11-records, under the heading EXPEDITION JOURNAL, the single entry reads "Mercurycarbon · 7/26" — one word, no separator. Source confirms the journal stores the biome KEY not its name (index.html:12940, `w: wbRoll ? String(wbRoll.k).slice(0,16) : ''`) and the row renders `<span class="k">Mercury</span><span>carbon · 7/26</span>` (index.html:23580–23581), which collapses to a single run of text at this width. The human-readable name exists: index.html:12633 defines `{k:'cratered', n:'Cratered world', ...}`, and every other surface uses the `.n` form.
Impact
"Expedition Journal" is the most narrative name in the interface — it promises a logbook, a record of where I have stood. The first and only line it ever showed me was a lowercase database token welded onto a planet name. It reads like the game forgot to finish the sentence, and it is the single strongest signal in the storyboard that the prose layer is thinner than it looks.
Suggested fix
Store and render the biome's display name (`wbRoll.n`) rather than its key, and write the row as a sentence rather than a two-column split: "Mercury — Carbon world · 7/26", or better, "Mercury · carbon plains · 26 Jul". At minimum add a separator between the two spans so they cannot fuse on narrow screens.
Reported by
lore-reader on iphone-16-pro-max

major A first-time player is shown the release changelog before the game pacing 4 testers · 4 devices
Evidence
State 02 is the second screen of the game: 'WHAT'S NEW IN THIS RELEASE / v1.7.0 The Forge' followed by 'ONE RARITY LADDER FOR EVERYTHING', 'THE FULL MATERIALS ECONOMY - 47 materials across five families', 'THE SEVEN COSMICS'. None of these terms has been introduced.
Impact
Every word is written for someone who played v1.6. To a new player it establishes, before they have done anything, that the game is more complicated than they can handle. Most likely tab-close point.
Suggested fix
Gate the release-notes modal on an existing save; show new explorers a three-line 'what you do in this game' card instead.
Reported by
cautious-newbie on iphone-se
Evidence
State 01 is ~120 words of lore filling 60% of the screen. State 02 is a full-screen changelog with four dense bullets referencing unseen systems. State 03 opens 'FIELD TRAINING 1 / 21'. Three full-screen text gates and four taps before one interactive element.
Impact
The number-one reason I close a browser game. A changelog is for returning players; to a new one it says 'this game is a lot of reading'.
Suggested fix
Gate release notes on a prior version in localStorage. Trim the name-gate lore to the one bolded line with a 'read more' disclosure.
Reported by
skimmer on iphone-15-pro
Evidence
ipad-land__02-release-notes.png: a fresh save, one tap after entering a name, gets a modal headed 'WHAT'S NEW IN THIS RELEASE — v1.7.0 The Forge, July 2026' with five dense bullets (rarity ladder, 47 materials, the seven cosmics, the Forge, Save Guardian) that scroll past the container edge. The only exit is CONTINUE at the bottom; there is no X.
Impact
A changelog is meaningless to someone who has never seen the previous version — every bullet references systems that do not exist for them yet. It is a full screen of reading and one forced tap inserted between naming my character and seeing the game, and it teaches me that this UI will spend my time freely.
Suggested fix
Gate the modal on a stored lastSeenVersion in localStorage. Absent (fresh save) means skip it entirely and go straight to Field Training; present and older means show it. Keep it reachable from the Guide for anyone who wants it.

major No tablet or large-viewport breakpoint — every panel is a phone-width column layout 4 testers · 5 devices
Evidence
08-atlas. Tapping the Star Atlas chip opens a ~300px popover pinned under the chip in the top-right. It contains a filter row (All / star 0 / flag / asterisk / 'Travel Home'), exactly one entry — 'Earth · Terran World' — and a footer. The panel is so narrow that 'Travel Home' wraps to two lines inside its own pill and the footer 'TAP AN ENTRY TO TRAVEL · FAVORITE · HOME' orphans 'HOME' onto a second line. There is no spatial view of anything: no star chart, no system diagram, no visited/unvisited state, no rarity colour.
Impact
For a player whose entire motivation is wandering and then getting back to the good bit they saw an hour ago, the Atlas is the game. Presenting it as a bookmarks list in a corner — one that Escape does not close — tells me the game does not actually expect me to navigate, only to advance. I have no way to answer 'where have I been' or 'what was near that ringed one'.
Suggested fix
On viewports >=700px give the Atlas its own panel at min(560px, 90vw) with a schematic chart pane (charted systems plotted by position, dot colour = rarity grade, filled = landed) beside the list, and widen the pills so 'Travel Home' and the footer stop wrapping. Add a 'recently visited' section so returning somewhere does not require having favourited it in advance.
Reported by
explorer on ipad-mini
Evidence
The stylesheet has exactly two width tiers: `@media (max-width:700px)` and `@media (min-width:701px)` (index.html lines 1423 and 1725). At 744px the iPad mini falls into the desktop bucket and inherits desktop's corner rails plus its fixed-width panels (#panel 300px, #records 318px) with only 44px of headroom over the phone breakpoint. Visible consequences: 03 and 04 — the 470px Field Training card overlaps the left rail, cutting the HP gauge (reads '100/100' with the bar and 'HP' hidden; compare 05, unobstructed, which reads '100/100 HP') and clipping the right edge of the Compendium chip. 11 and 16 — the Records and Notifications popovers land on top of the survey card and are sliced by the bottom of the screen mid-row (Records' 'ENGINEERING' row and the Notifications list's sixth entry are both cut). 14 — Settings covers the survey card's title so it reads 'ercury / ATERED WORLD'. Meanwhile in 05 the lower ~40% of the 1133px-tall screen is empty black.
Impact
The release notes promise 'On phones everything docks into two even rows at your thumbs' and desktop gets a designed command line, but the tablet gets neither — it gets desktop furniture at almost phone width. Every panel I open lands on top of the thing I was reading, and half the screen stays empty the whole time. It reads as a size nobody looked at.
Suggested fix
Add a 701–900px tier. Pin the training card below the rails (or dodge it downward) instead of centering it over them; cap corner popovers at `max-height: calc(100dvh - var(--topbar-h) - 120px)` so they stop being guillotined by the bottom bar; and let panels claim the empty vertical band — a two-row layout with the survey card upper-right and utility panels lower-left would use the space that is currently black.
Reported by
explorer on ipad-mini
Evidence
07-planetside. The panorama panel occupies roughly the middle quarter of the 1133px-tall viewport; above it is empty board and below it two toasts sitting on the survey card. A 'Full screen' button and a 'Save postcard' button sit under the image, and the caption reads 'LOCAL DAY — TAP TO CONTINUE · TAP TO ZOOM'.
Impact
This picture is the single best thing in the storyboard and the entire reason I would keep playing, and it is served at postage-stamp size on a device whose whole selling point is a big bright screen held in two hands. The full-size version exists one tap away, which makes the small default feel like an oversight rather than a choice. It also undercuts 'Save postcard' — I want to be moved before I want to share.
Suggested fix
On portrait tablets let the vista span the full panel width and take at least 55% of viewport height by default, with the buttons overlaid on the image rather than stacked beneath it. Consider making full-screen the default presentation at >=700px portrait and demoting the button to 'Exit full screen'.

major Tooltips have no collision awareness and cover what they describe layout 3 testers · 3 devices
Evidence
Three separate instances. ultrawide__11-records.png: the tooltip 'The Records board — your rarity ladder and every achievement shelf.' covers the Records panel's own last two rows — 'ENGINEERING 0/12 EXPAND' and 'CONQUEST 0/7 EXPAND' are legible only as 'ENG…' and 'CON…'. ultrawide__16-notifications.png: the tooltip 'Every toast lands here too — nothing is missed.' covers the final notification entry. ultrawide__15-guide.png: clicking ? shows only 'Celestial Frontier · v1.7.0 (build 4264b2e) ›' — the popover's actual '🧭 Open the Guide' button (index.html line 18211) is completely hidden beneath the tooltip 'Guide to the Universe — every system explained.' Root cause is that both the panels and their tooltips are anchored to the same bottom-right corner (#codex/#log right:18px, #setpanel bottom:58px, help popover above the ? button).
Impact
The Guide case is the bad one — the ? button appears to do nothing but print a build number, so a new player would conclude the Guide is broken and never open it. The Records/Notifications cases silently hide real content. All three happen with 800px of unused vertical space above the panel and 3,100px of unused width beside it.
Suggested fix
Flip tooltips to render above their trigger when the trigger is in the bottom 25% of the viewport, and give them a higher z-index than nothing — better, suppress the trigger's tooltip entirely while its own popover/panel is open.
Reported by
explorer on ultrawide
Evidence
showTip (index.html:18236-18248) positions the bubble with `y = r.top - bh - 8`, clamped only against the viewport (`clamp(x, 8, W-bw-8)` and `if(y<8) y=min(H-bh-8, r.bottom+8)`). It never checks what is already on screen. Three confirmed collisions at 720: (1) laptop-720__11-records.png — the bubble 'The Records board — your rarity ladder and every achievement shelf.' sits at y~605-660 directly over the Records panel's last row, hiding the WORLDS achievement line and its EXPAND button; the dock button that spawned it is at y~671 and `#records` is `bottom:60px` (index.html:1745), so the bubble lands inside the panel by construction. (2) laptop-720__16-notifications.png — 'Every toast lands here too — nothing is missed.' covers the fifth notification ('Expedition Charters'). (3) laptop-720__12-charters.png — the four-line Charters bubble occupies y~17-100 at top-left and completely hides the 'AUDITOR — CADET' nameplate and the 100/100 HP bar, both of which are plainly visible at those coordinates in every other laptop-720 screenshot.
Impact
The tooltip for a button is drawn on top of the content that button just revealed, so hovering to find out what a board does destroys the bottom of that board. The Charters case is worse than cosmetic: HP is the stat that gets you killed, and browsing quests blanks it out for as long as the cursor rests on the button. At 720 the panels are shorter (`#records` max-height resolves to ~440px here versus 540px at 1080) so a ~55px bubble eats a larger share of them.
Suggested fix
In showTip, get the bounding rects of any visible panel and flip or nudge the bubble to a side that does not intersect one; failing that, suppress the tooltip entirely while its own panel is open (`if(p.open()) return` for the matching PANELS entry) and clamp it away from the `#hud-left`/`#hpwrap` region.

Frame 02 shows the release-notes modal, whose keyboard bullet at index.html:18679 reads '⌨ KEYBOARD SUPPORT — Settings, Compendium, Binder, Star Atlas, and Guide entries are tabbable and fire on Enter or Space, each with a visible focus ring.' The game board is silently absent from that list. The focus ring it advertises is a single rule at 1579 — [role="button"]:focus-visible{outline:1px solid rgba(240,200,110,0.85)} — 1px, below the 2px perimeter WCAG 2.2 asks for, and scoped only to role="button", so it never applies to the native <button> elements inside the survey card, Shipyard or Atlas rows.
Impact
The release-notes bullet is the second screen a new player sees. It reads as 'keyboard support shipped', so I stopped looking for a settings toggle or a key list — and only worked out an hour of tabbing later that the board itself was never in scope. Suggested fix
Reword the release-notes bullet to state plainly what is and is not keyboard-operable until the board is fixed. Rewrite HINTS and the Atlas hint to name keys next to pointer verbs ('Arrow keys or hover to preview · Enter or click to survey · +/− or scroll to land'). Thicken the focus outline to 2px and broaden the selector to a:focus-visible, button:focus-visible, [tabindex]:focus-visible, [role="button"]:focus-visible.

Every row gives an exact input quantity and a line of flavour where the output spec should be — no yield quantity, no stat delta, no unlock, no craft time. Source (_fabHTML, ~line 20868) renders name + it.d + cost bits and nothing else. Contrast state 12, where Charters do state rewards numerically ('+15', '+10 · Pays gear: Miner's Headlamp') — the game clearly can do this.
Impact
Cost without benefit is an unpriceable decision. I have 1 Iron; spending it on a Plate versus a Frame is a coin flip because neither tells me what it buys. That kills the entire optimisation loop the materials economy exists to support.
Suggested fix
Add a benefit line under each recipe's cost line, same treatment: 'makes 1x Iron Plate — feeds Hull Plating (T2), Cargo Rack (T2)' for intermediates, and the actual stat/affix roll for anything with a slot. Where an item is purely an ingredient, list its downstream consumers (ITEMS already knows them — _matUses computes exactly this list for materials).

lore-reader on iphone-16-pro-max

The twelve testers

Each played the same build as a distinct persona on a distinct device, and scored it in their own terms.

1.5 accessibility desktop-1080 · 1920×1080 would stop
“I can tab to the Shipyard, the Atlas and every setting you shipped — but the sky itself is a canvas marked aria-hidden that only answers a mouse wheel, so I got a name, a tutorial, and nowhere to go.”
There is a real, careful accessibility effort in the chrome — tooltips that fire on keyboard focus, a focus-restore helper after re-renders, reduced-motion support, a Text size / Text tone / Font panel — and none of it reaches the actual game. Surveying, landing, panning, zooming and even leaving a planet are gated behind hover, click and mouse-wheel with no key behind any of them, and the canvas is explicitly marked aria-hidden="true" role="presentation", so a screen reader is told the universe does not exist. I named my explorer, sat through the offer of a 21-step Field Training, arrived in Sol, read '8 worlds orbit a yellow sun-like star' — and then had nothing to press. Tabbing through the panels to read about a game I cannot play is not fun; it is a museum tour of a locked building.

High point

Tabbing to the Star Atlas chip and having its tooltip appear on focus rather than only on hover — with a deliberate guard so a pointer-driven focus stays quiet. Someone on this team has used a keyboard on purpose.

Low point

Reading the permanent hint bar — 'Hover a planet to preview · click to survey · scroll in to land' — and realising all three verbs in the core loop are mouse gestures, that the storyboard's own 'survey card' frame shows no card, and that the Planetside frame is simply missing from this device's run.

Where they got lost

  • After Field Training the only instruction on screen is 'Hover a planet to preview · click to survey · scroll in to land'. None of the three verbs has a key behind it, and nothing else on screen suggests what I should press instead. I sat at the Sol map with focus on the Charters chip and no idea what my next keystroke was supposed to be.

  • Reset Game is a proper two-step: the destructive button swaps itself out for a confirm row that spells out what is lost, and reopening Settings resets that view (resetSettingsView, index.html:23152) so a stale armed confirm can never be clicked by accident.

The endgame the intro spent two paragraphs promising me turns out to be a nine-row list of the same string.

Where they got lost

  • Which rank am I? The header says AUDITOR — CADET and the Prime Codex says WANDERER, on screens I can flip between in one tap, with nothing telling me these are two different ladders.
  • What is "the order"? Field Training mentions it twice — "The order asks one thing of every new Pathfinder", "Practice specimens return to the order" — as if I already know. It is lowercase, unnamed, and never appears again in any of the sixteen screens. It is the only institution in the game and I cannot tell if it is a faction, a guild, or a typo.
  • What is the Deep Field? The Prime Codex says "Void and Prism far past the Deep Field" as though it is a known landmark. Nothing before it introduces the term, and it does not appear on the system map, the Atlas or the Guide.
  • Am I on a cratered world or a carbon world? The card and the landing screen disagree, and the journal sides with the landing screen.

What worked

  • The opening invocation is the real thing: "one small world, a borrowed ship, and a whole sky that has never learned your name" and the closing line "You cannot finish the infinite. You can master it." That is a thesis statement, not a tagline, and the Prime Codex text on 13 keeps faith with it almost word for word.
  • "Sol is yours to learn — the rest of the sky is charts and longing" (12-charters). Best sentence in the build. It does worldbuilding, motivation and pacing in eleven words.
  • The Shipyard item list (10-shipyard) is hand-written all the way down and never repeats a rhythm: "Rolled hull stock — the frontier is built on it", "Chromium-steel truss — light enough, unbreakable enough", "Fluorite-glass eye for instruments", "Filament cloth cracked from methane — suits begin here", "Slush of stabilized ices". And "A BARE HULL ON CHEMICAL THRUSTERS — BUILD HER OUT BELOW" gets the ship its pronoun.

The shape of the problem. The page itself loads in 791ms, but the name gate isn't usable for another ~2–3s of intro animation, and then three full-screen gates stand between the player and the map: name entry, the release changelog, and the training prompt. That is five interactions minimum. Even a bot that never reads takes 4.1s; the fleet median is 11.8s, and 54% of 13-second sessions never took a single gameplay action — they spent the whole session in onboarding. Skipping training saves only 2.4s, because the changelog and name gate are unskippable either way.

Performance

Measured in isolation — one device at a time, nothing else running, three interleaved repeats each, sampled at steady state on the system map. Headless Chromium with GPU disabled on a 2-core VM, so real hardware will do better; the useful signal is the trend against backing-store size.

A correction worth recording. An earlier pass reported 11 fps and 60% jank on several devices. That was this harness's own in-page layout audit running during measurement, not the game. Re-measured cleanly, the worst case is 45 fps. The bad numbers were an instrumentation artefact and have been discarded.

JavaScript errors

None. Across every fleet session and all 21 device sweeps, the game threw no uncaught exceptions and no unhandled promise rejections. For a 24,000-line single-file build driven by adversarial bots, that is a genuinely good result.

Reported but not confirmed1

Claims a tester made that I could not reproduce. Recorded here rather than dropped silently, because knowing what isn't broken is worth as much as knowing what is.

not confirmed Tapping a planet does not open the survey card on tablet and desktop viewportsspeedrunner / ipad-land
Original claim
ipad-land__06-survey-card.png is captured as the survey-card state but shows only the unchanged system map with two toasts — no card, no planet selected, no visible response to the tap. The identical step on galaxy-s21__06-survey-card.png renders a full Mercury card ('CRATERED WORLD', + ADD TO STAR ATLAS / LAND / SHARE THIS DISCOVERY). The pattern holds across the fleet: ipad-land, ipad-10, desktop-1080 and desktop-1440 all show no card at state 06 and have no 07-planetside frame on disk at all, while galaxy-fold and galaxy-s21 show the card and do have 07-planetside. Source note: the tap hit-test at index.html:5108 matches on p.r with a touch-padded minimum of 16*PICK_F = 22.4px radius (index.html:2161, :7082), so the target is nominally 44.8px across even though Earth draws at roughly 11 CSS px here — the miss is not simply a too-small target.
What I found
Not reproducible. Traced to this harness: the bot clicked coordinates captured up to a second earlier, and planets orbit. Measured drift is ~28px/second at default zoom while a planet disc is ~8–12px, so a stale click misses. Phones appeared unaffected only because touch taps get a 1.4× pick radius. Replaced by the verified drift finding below.
